summary: This resolution sets the terms for House consideration of the Senate amendment to H.R. 5371 by allowing a motion to concur, waiving points of order, limiting debate to one hour equally divided, and ordering the previous question.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is purely procedural, enabling House consideration of a continuing resolution (CR) for FY2026 appropriations. A CR maintains existing spending levels without new expansions or reductions, so the bill has no directional impact on government spending.
The bill text contains no provisions related to tax policy, rates, or revenue measures.
No provisions address healthcare funding, coverage, or regulation.
No provisions relate to firearms, regulations, or rights.
No provisions address immigration policy, borders, or pathways.
No provisions address reproductive rights or restrictions.
While a CR would continue baseline defense funding, the resolution itself makes no changes to military spending levels or policy.
No provisions address environmental regulations or protections.
No provisions alter welfare, entitlements, or safety-net programs.
No provisions address education funding or policy.
No provisions relate to drug enforcement or decriminalization.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
A CR continues existing deficit trajectories without new borrowing authority or debt-reduction measures; the resolution itself is neutral.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or restrictions.
No provisions address foreign assistance levels.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or reforms.
No provisions address technology regulation or data privacy.
No provisions address worker protections or union rights.
No provisions address religious exemptions or civil-rights priorities.
